book.title: The Geometry of Flow
book.sub: Everything Passes Through the Thin Part
blurb: The world is a circulation system—and so are you.
A ship wedges sideways in the Suez Canal. A coffee shop staffs the wrong weekend. A phrase becomes so charged that people stop hearing the words inside it. At first, these events appear unrelated.
Pull the camera back, and they reveal the same shape.
In The Geometry of Flow, Bob Cavin III braids canals, cables, currencies, borders, attention, grief, and presence into a single inquiry: What happens when everything must pass through a narrow place?

Global trade compresses through straits and chokepoints. Information travels through undersea cables and privately controlled platforms. A human life narrows through the present moment—the thin point where attention becomes experience.
Through creative nonfiction, systems thinking, and philosophical reflection, this book explores:

list: why borders explain possession while flow explains movement
how pressure creates rerouting rather than true stoppage
why efficiency can make systems fragile
what grief can teach us about resilience
why presence is not capturing a moment, but allowing it to pass through us completely
how the spaces between notes, words, people, and moments become the places where meaning is made

blurb: This is not a policy argument, a productivity manual, or a field guide. It is an essay about learning to see the outer world and the inner life as two maps of the same terrain.
Because the answer—at the scale of a civilization and at the scale of a Tuesday—is not a better wall.
